draft.title: Urbanisation
card: Urbanisation is the growing share of a country's or the world's people who live in cities and towns. It is measured as a percentage, not as a head count.
More than half the world's people now live in urban areas. The share is still rising in most regions.
Cities can grow or shrink without urbanisation if rural areas change at the same rate. Urbanisation means the urban share goes up, so the rural share goes down.
People moving from rural areas into cities adds to urban growth.
draft.remember: Urbanisation is a rising urban share of the population, not just a bigger city.

a.q: A country's census data are compared over time. Which change shows urbanisation?
opts: Urban share of people rises from 50% to 60%
Urban and rural populations both grow by 10%
Rural share of people rises from 40% to 50%
Urban and rural populations both fall by 5%
a.why: Urbanisation is a rising urban share, so a move from 50% to 60% shows it. If urban and rural populations both grow by 10%, cities get bigger but the urban share stays the same, so there is no urbanisation.
a.clue: Compare the people in cities with the whole population.

b.q: Country X had 10 million people, with 5 million in cities. Later it had 12 million, with 6 million in cities. What happened to urbanisation?
opts: It did not rise, as the urban share stayed at 50%
It rose, as the urban population grew by a million
It fell, as the total population grew by 2 million
It rose, as more people lived in cities than before
b.why: Urban share was 5 ÷ 10 = 50% and then 6 ÷ 12 = 50%. The share did not change, so there was no urbanisation even though cities grew. The option about a larger urban population is tempting, but urbanisation is about share.
b.clue: Work out the urban share before and after.

a.best: Urban share of people rises from 50% to 60%

b.best: It did not rise, as the urban share stayed at 50%
